answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, transferable token before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independent audits confirm fraud. Splitting one attacker into a thousand identities does not multiply influence for free: each identity needs its own bond, and detected fakes lose capital. The rule is not proof of personhood, and a wealthy attacker can still pay, but it makes large-scale Sybil attacks costly and exposes more funds to seizure. A walnut-sized stake, an ocean of accounts, or a comet-bright reputation cannot bypass that arithmetic.
